qa_reviewer_comment: Clean file. KYC current, red flags correctly assessed against documented income pattern, no RFI needed and correctly not sent, clearance fully supported by the account history reviewed.

Disposition itself is sound, but two things drag this down: the RFI added a week of processing delay and customer friction for information the file already contained, and the case notes don't explain why the RFI was sent given the existing documentation. Coaching point: check the file for existing supporting documentation before sending an RFI, and if one is sent anyway, document why.
Thorough PEP onboarding file. EDD, source-of-wealth documentation, adverse media, and escalation for sign-off are all present and well-documented.

Escalation decision itself was correct and timely, but the file needs a written rationale, not just a timestamp — an examiner reviewing this file six months from now has no way to reconstruct why this was escalated. Coaching point: every escalation needs 2-3 sentences of documented reasoning, even when the outcome is clearly correct.
Excellent SAR file — clear narrative, well-documented pattern, correctly escalated and filed.

Critical finding: the RFI response was accepted at face value without cross-referencing the business activity already documented in the KYC record, which describes a materially different business purpose. This is exactly the kind of inconsistency an RFI review exists to catch. Should have been escalated for further review; instead the case was closed. File must be reopened and reviewed by a senior investigator.

Critical finding: the case tool's own link-analysis panel showed the same funds moving through two related accounts within 48 hours, and this was not reviewed. This is not a subtle miss — the linkage was visible in a standard part of the case tool. File must be reopened; recommend refresher training on the link-analysis feature for this analyst.

Underlying decision to continue the relationship is well-supported, but two things need tightening: the expired beneficial-owner ID should have been flagged for refresh, and the written rationale for continuing the relationship is lighter than our high-risk EDD standard. Coaching point, not a rework — the analytical conclusion itself is sound.

Critical finding: a confirmed regulatory-action adverse media hit was dismissed with a one-line note and no documented analysis. Policy requires MLRO escalation for any confirmed regulatory-action hit; this did not happen. Clearing this file is not supportable on the documentation present. Must be reopened and escalated immediately.

Multiple non-critical gaps compound into a weak file: no documented comparison against account history, typology indicators only partially noted rather than walked through, and no risk-rating cross-check. Scored as a non-critical FAIL rather than a critical failure because the underlying transaction pattern, independently re-reviewed, does not itself appear to meet the threshold for escalation — the disposition reached is probably right, but the file as written doesn't demonstrate that, which is itself the deficiency. Requires rework and refresher coaching on documentation standards.
